chunks: 1477 - Saʿd ibn Saʿd narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام:
Regarding a traveler to Mecca and elsewhere: is the salat of the two Eids, al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā, incumbent upon him? He said: "Yes, except at Minā on the Day of Sacrifice."

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eids, meaning Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler, the person in a state of journey
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the location excluded in this ruling
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the sacred city and destination mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice, referring to Eid al-Aḍḥā

ai.seo_question: Is a traveler required to perform the Eid prayer in Mecca or elsewhere?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the salat of Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā for a traveler. It indicates that the traveler is to perform the Eid prayer, except in Minā on the Day of Sacrifice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1477 - Sa'd ibn Sa'd narrated from al-Ridha (as) regarding a traveler to Mecca or elsewhere, asking if the traveler is obligated to perform the Eid prayers (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha).
He (Imam (as)) said: "Yes, except in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha)."
